n933d9f0c876b: van Grinsven et al. combine tenfold expansion microscopy with a volumetric fluorescence averaging tool to map the human airway basal body at nanoscale resolution. They resolve the 3D organization of more than 20 proteins and assess the function of a subset of proteins in the organization of the apical microtubule network.
n33be42edc29c: Floral rewards and signals must be coordinated to attract pollinators, but the underlying genetic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using melon as a model system, this study reveals how the developmental regulator YAB5 coordinates nectar production, flower opening, and floral signals to promote bee visitation.
nab486173fb9d: Single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary input of viral genomes, which varies with different viruses and cell types. We show that supra-unitary viral genome quantities, independently of viral protein synthesis, activate negative feedback regulators of RIG-I, MDA-5, and PKR, suppressing the innate immune response and allowing replication.
ned99384d97a9: Kadoki et al. developed GPCR-seq, a high-throughput platform to identify how the gut senses environmental chemicals. They discovered gut microbial products that activate intestinal receptors, triggering serotonin release or linking to inflammatory bowel disease. This work provides a scalable template for decoding how host-microbe communication influences human health.
n385f8cd6fee0: Liu et al. present MorphX, an interpretable deep learning framework that decodes cancer prognosis from whole-slide histological images and reveals morphological biomarkers. Across independent cohorts, MorphX identifies eight morphology-based biomarkers, supporting trustworthy, transparent, AI-driven precision oncology.
n8a5bb46bc0a2: Diao and colleagues identify uPAR as a shared marker of pathogenic macrophage and fibro-adipogenic progenitor subsets in DMD. Selective depletion of these cells by uPAR CAR T cells remodels the dystrophic muscle niche, restores muscle regeneration, and improves limb and respiratory muscle function in preclinical murine models of DMD.
n4a738dee8eb5: Zhou et al. show VEGFR-1 signaling in intestinal Tfh cells is essential for immune surveillance. Its loss impairs IgA immunity, allowing a gut bacterium to deplete taurine, impair fat burning, and drive obesity. Restoring this axis offers an immune-based strategy for metabolic disorders.
na381f7f9a134: The rising incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) challenges existing paradigms of tumorigenesis. Classical models based on cumulative mutational burden, environmental exposure, and hereditary predisposition fail to explain the emergence of malignancy in individuals under 50 years of age. In this review, we propose that EOCRC may be driven by accelerated biological aging and review how core aging processes are prematurely activated in EOCRC. Importantly, these alterations extend beyond the tumor microenvironment and are present in circulating immune cells and inflammatory mediators. We propose that EOCRC develops prematurely in response to environmental, metabolic, genetic, and related factors that systemically accelerate biological aging. This approach reconciles the origin of EOCRC with traditional models of tumorigenesis, while highlighting novel opportunities for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic intervention.
n4076c02a770c: The space surrounding the body where physical interactions with external stimuli occur is referred to as peripersonal space (PPS). Traditionally conceived as a spatial construct, PPS is better understood as a neural representation that integrates bodily inputs with external cues to predict body–object interactions. After summarizing its multisensory, motor, and plastic properties, this review draws on computational models to examine how PPS captures statistical regularities of body–object interactions. This predictive function may position PPS as an interface between self and environment, contributing to minimal self-consciousness and its alterations across states of consciousness and neuropsychiatric conditions. Recent findings extend this framework to the inner body, suggesting that interoceptive signals shape PPS and that PPS-related processing may influence immune responses.
nb940fd64b2d9: Hundreds to thousands of dinoflagellate symbionts (Amphidinium sp., 10–20 μm in size) move up to hundreds of micrometers inside the tissue of their acoel worm hosts (Waminoa sp., millimeters in size). Host actin machinery is primarily responsible for driving symbiont mobility at speeds around 1 μm/s, and symbionts move inside ribbon-like host cells (∼200 nm thin), which stretch to accommodate symbionts moving through them.
n109a2c0ea443: By using multimodal spatial transcriptomics to measure somatic repeat expansion, huntingtin pathology, and transcriptional profile in every cell of intact tissue sections, we identify in the Huntington’s disease cortex that large somatic CAG repeat expansions are linked to the selective loss of L5–6 NP and L6b deep-layer excitatory neurons. Intranuclear inclusions of huntingtin were most prevalent at intermediate somatic repeat expansions and were associated with broader transcriptional changes than somatic repeat expansion alone.
n20b50cc39fd7: Single-cell-resolution analysis of brain tissue in Huntington's disease (HD) reveals that cortical and striatal neurons pass through analogous biological changes, each initiated by a neuron's own expanding DNA repeat. In cortical neurons, as in striatal neurons, the DNA repeat expands somatically over decades (phases A and B) and becomes toxic at about 150 CAGs, initiating cell-identity erosion (phase C), the formation of nuclear inclusions of aggregated HTT protein, a derepression crisis (phase D), and then death of the neuron.
n42a079016a7e: Luo et al. review uncertainty quantification in medical AI from a clinical perspective and propose a practical roadmap for translating uncertainty estimates into meaningful action. They highlight the need to validate uncertainty against clinically relevant errors and embed its use within real-world workflows and governance.
n58deec015ebc: Lin et al. identified a distinct EPCR+CD150− hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) subset termed LT-HSC2. It is characterized by a prominent dormancy status during homeostasis that surpasses EPCR+CD150+ LT-HSC1. LT-HSC2s exhibit all LT-HSC hallmarks including extensive capacity to self-renew and serial multi-lineage reconstitution capacity at bulk and single-cell level.
n9ab3675c5ce3: Qiu and colleagues revealed that the endothelial potential of adult EPDCs is unlocked by an improved electroconductive microenvironment rebuilt through cardiac electroconductive-matched patches. Using lineage tracing and scRNA-seq, they explored how electroconductive microenvironment guides EPDCs into functional vessels, promoting cardiac repair post-MI.
nc0550329ab56: Human tissue models are rewriting preclinical science. Tavakol et al. examine how converging cell biology and bioengineering can close translational gaps, overcome reproducibility and regulatory hurdles, and, with synthetic biology, multi-omics, and AI, turn organoids and organs-on-a-chip into foundational platforms for personalized medicine, drug discovery, and regenerative therapies.
n3b1c91b82d9c: PD-L1 is generally considered to suppress immune responses. However, Akama-Garren et al. reveal an immunogenic role for PD-L1 in germinal centers. Expressed on B cell zone reticular cells, including follicular dendritic cells, PD-L1 promotes humoral immunity by restraining a subset of T follicular helper cells that promotes T follicular regulatory cell development.
n51238299c050: Bispecific PD-L1×4-1BB antibodies under clinical development enhance antitumor T cell responses. Luri-Rey et al. find that the efficacy of PD-L1×4-1BB antibodies relies on PD-L1-expressing type 1 conventional dendritic cells, which integrate antigen cross-presentation, IL-12, and 4-1BB costimulation to promote efficacious T cell-mediated antitumor immunity.
nc86639d7d0fd: Khamina, Wunsch et al. use a bacterial effector protein to isolate and determine the structure of V-ATPase from an important model plant. The structure reveals posttranslational modifications that are specific to the plant enzyme, and interactions with an activity-modulating protein similar to interactions described previously for mammalian and fungal V-ATPases.
n600496a506a7: Plants growing in fluctuating environments require dynamic coordination between carbon availability and growth–stress decisions. Trehalose-6-phosphate (Tre6P), a sugar signal linked to sucrose status, helps coordinate these decisions by regulating SUCROSE NON-FERMENTING 1-RELATED KINASE 1 (SnRK1)- and TARGET OF RAPAMYCIN (TOR)-dependent growth programs. Here, we synthesize recent advances in photosynthetic carbon dynamics, carbon sensing, and Tre6P–SnRK1–TOR signaling, highlighting emerging regulatory layers including Class II TREHALOSE PHOSPHATE SYNTHASE proteins, SnRK1 compartmentalization, and stress-associated TOR regulation. We further discuss how different photosynthetic strategies of carbon fixation, including C3, C4, and crassulacean acid metabolism, as well as UV-B signaling through UV RESISTANCE LOCUS 8, influence carbon–energy signaling. Finally, we outline unresolved questions relevant to crop resilience under fluctuating environments.
n9f1e8b930345: More than a century after observations linking muscular activity to reduced cancer risk, exercise oncology has progressed from epidemiological association to interventional evidence. Large cohort studies associate physical activity with reduced cancer incidence and mortality, and a Phase 3 randomized trial now demonstrates cancer-specific survival benefits of structured exercise. In parallel, preclinical and emerging human studies provide mechanistic insight into how exercise may modulate tumor biology, including effects on immune surveillance, vascular function, metabolism, and systemic signaling. Despite these advances, gaps remain—notably, the limited integration of exercise variables into oncology trials and sparse mechanistic data from patients, particularly in pediatric cancers. This opinion article synthesizes recent clinical and mechanistic advances and outlines priorities for biologically informed integration of exercise into cancer research and the standard of care.
n564700a87d42: Past research has long hinted at a connection between microtubules and the growth of the heart. Here, we highlight a new role for microtubules in directing cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by altering protein translation and intercellular adhesion and discuss how these findings illuminate open questions in cardiac remodeling.
n955f6320c073: Researchers and laypeople commonly assume that romantic attraction depends, at least in part, on whether potential partners possess the traits that a person says they want. Yet recent studies suggest that such preference-matching effects (Preference × Trait statistical interactions) are often surprisingly small or even absent. Possible psychological explanations include (i) mate choice is multivariate, and so the matching effect for any given trait is heavily constrained, and (ii) traits permit flexible interpretations, in that the same trait can be interpreted differently depending on the partner to whom the trait belongs. Compatibility may derive not mainly from the matching of preferences and traits but rather from the way that two people recurrently extend and build upon shared positive experiences over time.
nd2f47578813f: The science of emotion increasingly relies on machine learning (ML) in the hope of making objective discoveries that resolve century-long debates. We examine research strategies in two main research traditions and show how confirmation bias can arise when theory-based hypotheses are evaluated using theory-laden sampling strategies, model specifications, and inferences. Each tradition manifests its theoretical differences in its ML methods, and, therefore, ML methods cannot settle those differences. The reciprocal relationships between starting assumptions, findings, and conclusions illustrate that ML investigations of emotion, like all scientific investigations, are never free from human experience and beliefs; however, they can be made less biased through a theory-aware research strategy to generate more justified knowledge about emotion.
nd9a61afca360: Deep coverage sequencing of 3,367 maize genomes reveals substantial contributions of rare variants to trait heritability and provides insights into how selection reshapes their contribution to complex traits.
n96c614aca21c: Adeluwa et al. developed TFXcan, a framework that predicts personalized transcription factor binding from genotype data across ∼700 transcription-factor-tissue pairs. Applied to PrCa risk, TFXcan identified specific transcription factors and coordinated programs of transcription factors that drive the disease at risk loci.
nf0dec56e2dc7: Ling et al. develop T-IDLESTCE, a T cell-targeted integration-deficient lentiviral vector that programs endogenous T cells to secrete TCEs in situ. TCE-secreting T cells infiltrate disease-relevant tissues, drive deep plasma cell depletion, and promote sustained ocular improvement in an autoimmune dry eye model.
n5f7c9c6c9004: A single-dose AAV-CRISPR therapy restores dystrophin in humanized DMD mice and achieves durable editing with manageable safety in non-human primates. In a first-in-human DMD trial, the therapy yields molecular evidence of muscle editing but reveals a fatal dose-dependent immune complication, highlighting the urgent need to expand the safety margin of systemic AAV-CRISPR treatments.
n321d65a73c25: Bispecific proteins often rely on flexible linkers that increase conformational heterogeneity. Qiu et al. present AlphaSync, a geometry-guided framework that integrates α-helical binders through helix sharing. The resulting Chimeraffibody retains HER2-albumin co-recognition while improving pharmacokinetics, tumor localization, and predicted immunogenicity liability.
n5e5e1f308020: Victori et al. present a mechanistic computational model of triple-negative breast cancer that integrates prior biological knowledge with patient data from the PARTNER clinical trial. These personalized tumor digital twins recapitulate treatment responses, identify mutational and transcriptomic response biomarkers, and recommend targeted therapies, highlighting their potential to support precision oncology.
nd4cb83348937: Our understanding of how commensal-specific CD4+ T cells respond to intestinal inflammation is limited. Pedersen et al. define the phenotypic diversity of human CD4+ T cells recognizing a defined Bacteroidales epitope across disease settings. This revealed a TMIGD2hi Th17 phenotype that expands in inflamed tissue. More broadly, this work underscores the malleability of microbiota-specific T cells during inflammatory bowel disease.
n43e5ac8bcbdf: Human brain cellular xenograft (HBCX) models are emerging as a system to study human brain physiology and pathology in vivo. Mancuso and colleagues discuss how HBCXs enable in vivo interrogation of human-specific brain cell biology, neuroimmunology, disease modeling, and genetic risk and their potential for functional genomics, therapeutic discovery, and preclinical assessment of cell-based therapies for central nervous system disorders.
n49ce1802fc96: Semen carries extracellular RNA that shapes early embryonic development, but how it reaches sperm is unclear. Mallen et al. show that amyloid fibrils in seminal fluid bind RNA, enter sperm, and deliver their cargo to the zygote at fertilization, where chaperones release it for translation.
n7d840c02543d: Viral RNA genomes fold into networks of compact structures, so their RNA sequences do more than carry genetic code. Hann et al. review how viral RNA structures control viral gene expression, replication, and immune evasion, revealing viruses as simple model systems for regulatory principles that also shape human gene expression.
nd01356427aa9: Grimsley et al. demonstrate that the 9-1-1 complex safeguards BRCA2-deficient cells from lethal ssDNA gap accumulation by suppressing PRIMPOL-dependent gap formation, restraining EXO1 degradation, and promoting POLζ-mediated filling. This identifies an ATR-independent 9-1-1 role in post-replicative repair and establishes gap length as a key determinant of repair pathway choice.
n5500283d0f9e: Obarska-Kosinska et al. combine cryo-electron tomography, AI-assisted modeling, and crosslinking mass spectrometry to build an extended model of the human nuclear pore. They identify five additional nucleoporins and show how the nuclear basket and TREX-2 complex are attached to the nuclear ring, revealing the spatial organization of mRNP export.
ncfbb2a8680c5: SCLC cell states dictate how cancer cells respond to metabolic stress, revealing how metabolic plasticity determines whether the cells undergo ferroptosis or apoptosis.
nfe13750d8766: Perforin is best known for delivering granzymes into tumor cells, but this study shows it has a second, independent killing function: it drives iron uptake and mitochondrial iron overload that trigger ferroptosis. This granzyme-independent pathway links cytotoxic immunity to iron metabolism, predicts patient response to checkpoint blockade, and points to iron supplementation as a possible lever for boosting anti-tumor immunity.
n61d02208bcea: Taurine levels increase with age in mice and humans. Boosting taurine levels even further in aged mice increases health span and dampens inflammation through its regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.
n2377cd61cdf0: Hasegawa et al. show that a class of bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) harbored by Bacteroidales species promote elimination of vancomycin-resistant enterococcus (VRE) in the presence of Lachnospiraceae bai+ bacteria. In the gut, bacteria producing this subclass of BSH eliminate and displace VRE through deoxycholic acid (DCA) production.
n9be88fb915a2: Activation of the NF-κB pathway triggers diverse inflammatory outcomes despite similar upstream signaling. Leão et al. show that Ser276 phosphorylation of the p65 subunit of NF-κB p65 promotes CBP/p300 recruitment, enabling latent enhancer engagement and activation, and revealing an enhancer-selection mechanism that controls a distinct gene expression program shaping inflammatory and antimicrobial immune responses.
ncbbafb751ad5: Verma, Zhu, et al. show that PARP1 promotes NAD+-dependent eviction of H2A-H2B dimers, generating oriented hexasomes with increased DNA accessibility. The H2A C-terminal tail supports this remodeling activity, linking PARP1-dependent nucleosome disassembly to cellular responses to DNA damage.
nd889b61b8f0d: Liu et al. enabled genome-wide clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) screening of primary human T cells in vivo and identified P2RY8 and GNAS through complementary readouts. We discuss how context shapes perturbation effects, and how readouts guide prioritization, with implications for T cell engineering in solid tumors.
n1ae40323b3c9: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have been a feature of stem cell research since the early 1990s. Despite long-standing questions concerning the identity, characteristics, physiological functions, and potential therapeutic uses of these cells, MSC studies are now published more frequently than those of any other stem cell type. Over the past decade, this increase in the MSC literature is attributable almost entirely to publications by scientists in China. Reviewing the history and present state of MSC research, we explore why this might be and propose steps that stakeholders in China and other countries might take to address what has become one of the more perplexing developments in contemporary stem cell research.
n08238d63a8dc: In the original article [1], I claimed that dependency grammar is the simplest theory of grammar. All theories of grammar have rules for connecting words together to make larger units. In dependency grammar, these connections are directly between words. In phrase structure grammars, there is slightly more structure than in dependency grammar, consisting of nonterminal categories for the connected elements, such as the noun phrase and the verb phrase. I argued that these two alternatives are somewhat interchangeable.
n8ca24e354535: Gibson advocates dependency grammar [1], contrasting it with constituency-based accounts that posit movement and phonologically null (unpronounced) syntactic elements [2,3]. Dependency grammar represents sentence structure through word-to-word relations, whereas constituency-based accounts represent sentence structure by grouping words into larger hierarchical constituents. Movement accounts for cases in which a constituent appears in one position but is interpreted in another. For example, in ‘Who did you call?’, ‘Who’ appears sentence-initially but is interpreted as the object of ‘call’; this is analysed as movement from the object position to the sentence-initial position.
n2a9671d09982: Dietary and microbial alterations increase susceptibility to irAEs by promoting IFN-γ-driven Treg fragility and cytotoxic tissue-resident T cell responses. Treg-specific disruption of IFN-γ signaling restores tissue homeostasis and reduces irAEs without compromising antitumor immunity, highlighting Treg stability as a potential therapeutic strategy for limiting checkpoint blockade toxicity.
n0d03cf13d960: The orphan transporter MCT6 is the route by which the meal- and exercise-associated metabolite Lac-Phe exits intestinal cells and enters the blood. Mice lacking gut MCT6 cannot maintain normal circulating Lac-Phe levels and exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss, establishing metabolite export as a regulatory node for systemic action.
n93e33a3888ad: Single-molecule imaging reveals that metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive, and it relies on the repeated recruitment of Pol α and Pol δ rather than their stable replisome association, thereby uncoupling leading- and lagging-strand synthesis.
n44dc0c893511: ER-associated protein degradation is central to organelle homeostasis, yet many regulatory components remain unknown. Liu et al. exploit the rapid turnover of short-lived proteins to identify TXNDC15 as a noncanonical MARCHF6-dependent ERAD factor that links proteostasis to lipid homeostasis, illustrating how rapid proteolysis can uncover hidden metabolic regulatory circuits.
na92d0f06a84e: Zhang et al. show that gut microbial inositol phosphate metabolism transduces feeding cues into intestinal diurnal rhythms through histone deacetylase 3. This pathway activates PGC-1α and enhances nutrient absorption during feeding, promoting juvenile growth during undernutrition but exacerbating obesity during overnutrition.
nc509c644270e: Fan et al. develop CXCR4-engineered hepatocyte cytoplasts integrated with Au-Pt nanorobots to deplete tumor lactate through gluconeogenesis. Lactate depletion suppresses repair-associated lactylation and impairs MRN-mediated DNA repair, while Au-Pt catalysis amplifies radiation-induced damage. This metabolic remodeling simultaneously alleviates immunosuppression and promotes systemic antitumor immunity.
n3a4e86a97ec8: The authors introduce a programmable synthetic biology framework for tissue construction from hiPSCs through subtractive multicellular engineering. By selectively removing undesired cells during development via synthetic apoptosis circuits, this approach enhances tissue maturation and refines morphogenesis across organoid and embryoid models.
n7cf87e6ade39: Delaney et al. show that HP1HPL-2 can silence genes and restrict organogenesis independently of histone H3K9 methylation and the major H3K9 HMT SETDBMET-2. HP1HPL-2 and SETDB1MET-2 form heterochromatic foci by binding distinct cofactors, and these foci, not H3K9me3, track with gene silencing and developmental control of organogenesis.
nfe431ec0d4b7: For decades, core knowledge accounts have proposed that early cognition is organized by innate, domain-specific conceptual or concept-like representations of objects, physical events, number, and agents. I propose a different starting point: infants’ behaviors may arise from domain-general attentional priors—evolutionarily shaped selection biases—interacting with perceptual mechanisms that organize information and support perceptual prediction, rather than from abstract, postperceptual representations. Attentional priors favor ecologically consequential information, including continuity, contact, and synchrony. When such information is disrupted, perceptual prediction error—rather than conceptual contradiction—may produce violation-of-expectation effects. Grounded in constraints on visual input and neural processing, this framework accounts for early successes and systematic failures, suggesting that development begins with perceptual-attentional mechanisms that shape selection, organization, prediction, and learning.
n967349073040: Selective pharmacological induction of ferroptosis in vivo has remained difficult. By developing the bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor KY0418, this work links systemic ferroptosis induction to tissue metabolic remodeling and demonstrates context-dependent suppression of tumor progression, including metastatic spread.
n7b0c3447276d: Roman and post-Roman Iberia was transformed by extensive mobility across the Mediterranean, with large-scale inputs from Eastern Mediterranean and North African populations reshaping its genetic landscape. During the migration period, Central-Northern European ancestry arrived largely through elite-associated groups that intermarried with local populations but did not replace the highly diverse population that had formed under Roman rule.
nbfd553ce57e8: Computational reconstruction, screening, and engineering of non-LTR retrotransposons uncovers elements, termed Gene Writers, that enable stable transgene integration in human cells using all-RNA delivery. After extensive characterization and optimization, Gene Writers is deployed to generate functional CAR-T cells in vivo in a humanized mouse model.
nae325db0b8d9: A multi-omic atlas of human T cell exhaustion reveals that dysfunctional T cells undergo broad remodeling of protein turnover and ubiquitin regulation that is not captured by transcriptomic analysis. The E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF166 regulates T cell persistence and anti-tumor function, highlighting proteostasis as a targetable axis for improving immunotherapy.
n2ecb17f72ebf: How proteasome function shapes ferroptosis sensitivity is poorly understood. Murray et al. demonstrate that proteasome inhibition enhances sensitivity to ferroptosis induced by direct inhibition of GPX4, while protecting against system xc− inhibitors. Sensitization to GPX4 inhibitors requires protein synthesis and is opposed by activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4).
n2339e7d6040f: Chen et al. identify rAcrIIA1, a phage-encoded chimeric crRNA-tracrRNA mimic that competitively blocks Cas9 guide loading and DNA interference. This reprogrammable RNA guide enables efficient genome editing, gene silencing, and diagnostics, with enhanced trans-cleavage activity.
n00b6524fcea4: Brown and colleagues review recent approaches to overcome limitations to AAV brain gene therapies from vector design through clinical implementation, highlighting how success and patient safety must consider routes of administration, target engagement, and dosing.
n3ebfeeea0033: Allogeneic transplants can trigger graft-versus-host disease and graft rejection. Lopes Souza et al. demonstrate that deletion of Ctps1 in T cells prevents GVHD and reduces skin rejection. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of CTPS1 improves survival in acute GVHD, highlighting CTPS1 as a promising therapeutic target for alloreactive T cell responses.
ne682a7838a0e: Mano and colleagues have developed a self-organized bone-like model by co-encapsulating stromal and monocytic cells in liquefied gelatin microcapsules. Their direct interaction effectively supports the emergence of osteoblast-, osteocyte-, and osteoclast-like phenotypes, facilitating cellular crosstalk and promoting mineralized matrix formation and turnover without the need for lineage-specific induction.
n17d0fc3971e8: Yu and colleagues reveal that hematopoietic stem cells employ Rbpms condensates to spatially restrict the translation elongation machinery. By slowing protein synthesis and ensuring proper protein folding, this mechanism preserves proteostasis, quiescence, and LT stem cell function.
nec311dcc22e4: Griffith et al. show that arginine methylation drives production of short mRNA isoforms in rapidly dividing cells by enabling PCF11 to assemble productively into the cleavage and polyadenylation machinery. PRMT inhibition globally lengthens 3′UTRs across cancer cells, organoids, and T cells, revealing a targetable link between methylation and alternative polyadenylation.
ne25968e1c5ad: Personalized cancer treatment requires stratification of patients based on biomarkers. Despite advances in biomarker-guided therapy, biomarkers are not always available or sufficient to predict treatment responses in individual patients. Functional ex vivo cancer models with the potential to assess therapeutic outcomes upfront have been developed but have not been implemented in clinical practice—despite accumulating evidence of their clinical relevance. This review describes how three essential steps in the development of personalized functional prediction tests (analytical validity, clinical validity, and clinical utility) should be combined in a multidisciplinary approach: Integrated Translational Co-design. This approach front-loads clinical utility and validation constraints into early analytical design decisions, so that biological fidelity, clinical implementation, and healthcare costs can be optimized from the start of assay development.
nbde709cdf629: Lipid droplet proteins can move from the endoplasmic reticulum to droplets through persistent membrane connections. A new single-molecule study reveals that accumulation is not only about access: protein sequence features tune residence on the droplet surface, revealing how confined mobility can lead to accumulation on the organelle (Mizrak et al.).
nf733d2ff08dd: Enhancing insulin secretion is a major therapeutic strategy for diabetes. Matsunaga et al. identify DPEU, a small molecule that promotes mitochondrial ATP export through VDACs to enhance glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Their findings establish VDAC-mediated ATP flux as a therapeutic mechanism for potentiating insulin secretion.
ne69a59f01bd5: van den Berg et al. show that the modular organization of bacterial immune systems can be exploited to discover phage defense systems. Their approach identifies three previously unknown systems in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, revealing distinct strategies against jumbo phages and an RM-like defense system with additional regulatory components.
n09c70fcdd09c: Koehler et al. demonstrate distinct physiological roles for GLP-1R and GLP-2R signaling in protecting the intestine from αCD3-induced enteropathy. Conversely, GLP-1R/GLP-2R agonists, administered separately or together, attenuate the heightened intestinal damage induced by T cell activation in mice with selective loss of intestinal proglucagon gene expression.
n340d0320c773: Exploiting ORFeome libraries with different C-terminal architectures, Grant et al. perform comparative stability profiling to identify a conditionally regulated C-degron pathway governed by the CTLHMuskelin E3 ligase complex. Its substrate AAMP is the human ortholog of yeast Sqt1 and acts similarly as a uL16 chaperone, connecting nutrient status to control of ribosome biogenesis.
ne30bda7b0cd6: Bryant et al. develop adaptamers, compact RNA switches that use FDA-approved drugs to control gene expression by co-opting endogenous RNA-editing machinery rather than relying on foreign proteins. In mice, this approach safely tuned a metabolic hormone to reverse obesity, pointing to a simpler path toward programmable, drug-controlled gene therapies.
n5732450a32e4: Modern-day group leaders are expected to excel not only in scientific research and teaching but also in leadership and in providing a safe and intellectually stimulating environment for the next generation of budding scientists. In this article, we explore the evolution of a modern-day group leader within and beyond the scientific community.
n182ebafe6f1a: Over the past few decades, the emergence of immunotherapy and single-target drugs has brought new promise to the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Yet the high heterogeneity of NSCLC leads to both primary and acquired resistance that neither sequential monotherapy nor empirical combinations can effectively overcome. In contrast to the conventional coadministration of two separate monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) feature a series of molecular engineering designs that confer inherent synergistic antitumor effects. We propose that a network pharmacology perspective can be adopted to understand the application of BsAbs in NSCLC and to guide their subsequent development.
ne4150f517cd9: The deregulated utilization of nutrients by tumors, first observed over a century ago, is recognized as a hallmark of cancer and continues to be exploited clinically to image neoplastic disease. Despite this historic focus on cancer cells and, more recently, their neighbors, metabolic reprogramming is not limited to the tumor microenvironment. Tumors also have the capacity to rewire the metabolism of cells throughout the body, including those at distant sites, often referred to as the tumor macroenvironment. Alterations in the metabolism of noncancerous tissues outside the local tumor ecosystem are gaining attention, but their origins and consequences remain incompletely defined. A deeper understanding of these changes may reveal previously unrecognized signatures of disease and unexplored opportunities for therapeutic intervention.
ne6205ca21080: Efforts to extinguish DEI provoke questions about the ongoing significance of diversity science. We argue that this evolving context makes such research increasingly pressing, and we pose four questions that this environment both calls for and newly allows research to answer. Such science remains indispensable to society’s capacity to manage social differences.
n3db1974dcaf1: isoUDCA, a female-enriched bile acid produced by a gut bacterial consortium favored by estrogen, promotes hepatic cholesterol handling and bile acid metabolism through SREBP2-STARD4-CYP7B1 signaling, thereby alleviating chronic liver injury.
n9eec5648cf3f: ʟ-Carnitine is a nonproteinogenic amino acid highly abundant in myocytes, and both excess ingestion of myocytes and myocyte necrosis are associated with systemic inflammation. Here, we find that the pyrin inflammasome senses extracellular ʟ-carnitine through the high-affinity carnitine transporter OCTN2 (SLC22A5) and this leads to IL-1β-mediated inflammation. Our findings position OCTN2 as a potential target to reduce inflammation from exogenous or endogenous sources of extracellular ʟ-carnitine.
n607a90cce48d: First-in-class selective chemical targeting of USP32 uncovers its role in endosomal ubiquitin signaling. Scherpe, Vermue et al. develop a covalent USP32 inhibitor and complementary activity-based probes that reveal known and new membrane trafficking substrates and enable direct interrogation of USP32 activity in cells.
n8dd83dcc1d12: Zhang et al. demonstrate that isobavachalcone targets the deubiquitinase OTUB1 to promote PD-L1 ubiquitination and degradation in cancer cells. This regulation enhances T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and reshapes the tumor immune microenvironment to suppress tumor growth.
n267c40d7607c: Luan et al. reveal that SOX2 condensates promote squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) progression by regulating chromatin organization and oncogene expression. The FDA-approved drug ixazomib selectively disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner, offering an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy with high translational potential.
nd9082dfcb53f: Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are emerging as important regulators of immunity in gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. Enriched in mucosal and hepatic tissues, MAIT cells recognize microbial-derived metabolites presented by MHC class I-related molecule MR1 and rapidly exert effector functions, including cytokine production and cytotoxicity. Across GI malignancies, including hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and esophageal cancers, MAIT cells display context-dependent roles shaped by the tumor microenvironment, microbiome, and immune signaling pathways. While they can mediate antitumor immunity, they frequently exhibit functional exhaustion or adopt pro-tumorigenic phenotypes. Therapeutic strategies aim to enhance MAIT cell activity, reverse dysfunction, and integrate them into combinatorial immunotherapy approaches. Understanding MAIT cell biology may enable their exploitation as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in GI cancers.
n031dbfdf0a8f: Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) is a DNA polymerase expressed in pre-B and pre-T cells that functions in V(D)J recombination to add random nucleotides in a template-independent (TI) mode at junctions between antigen receptor gene segments. However, cellular, biochemical, and structural studies have also revealed a significant, short-length, template-dependent (TD) mode of TdT, in which it takes instructions from a template strand across a double-strand break. Here, we propose that this can occur through an intrachain fold-back synthesis to generate the short inverted repeats at V(D)J recombination junctions observed in early human lymphoid cells and within the adult human antigen receptor repertoire. This duality is also relevant to the functional and structural flexibility observed during the DNA repair process known as nonhomologous DNA end joining (NHEJ).
nd6870fce4a78: Jiang et al. show that Akkermansia muciniphila reshapes the tumor immune environment to overcome PD-1 resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC). Mechanistic studies and a phase 1 trial support gut microbiome modulation as a promising strategy to improve immunotherapy in this common treatment-resistant disease.
n9136ccfb3367: Li et al. show that activated CAR-T cells upregulate NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs), rendering them susceptible to NK cells. Overexpressing NKG2D shields endogenous ligands and harnesses tumor NKG2DLs for costimulation, thereby enhancing CAR-T cell persistence, tumor infiltration, and antitumor efficacy across multiple models.
nb03ad83957ab: Liu et al. demonstrate that high membrane magnesium transporter 1 (MMGT1) expression promotes immune evasion via a senescence-associated secretory phenotype that induces CD8+ T cells exhaustion. Targeting MMGT1 represents a promising strategy to improve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy.
nf2ef18422680: Wang et al. generate vascularized pancreatic islet organoids (VPIOs) containing organotypic vascular networks exhibiting endothelial fenestration. Vascularization enhances β cell maturation in vitro and survival under hypoxia. Following transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs establish functional connections with the host vasculature and effectively restore normoglycemia.
n5a881812522f: Ginhoux, Mulder, Arcila-Barrera, and Amit argue that macrophage identity is best understood not as a set of discrete subsets or a binary M1/M2 axis but as combinations of modular gene programs. They propose an extensible, program-based classification of macrophage states and discuss how it reframes macrophage-directed therapy from targeting individual checkpoints toward program-level reprogramming.
nc9f8f2a7a2d7: Srivastava et al. show that de novo-designed protein binders can selectively recognize the closed state of HSP90. The binders stabilize this conformation and provide new tools to study the HSP90 chaperone cycle and suggest a potential approach to HSP90 inhibition.
nfb8e8d3df4dc: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a bioactive gas essential for several physiologically important biological processes, including metabolism, acid–base homoeostasis, and chemosensing. CO2 can directly modulate these processes by stimulating or inhibiting specific cell signalling pathways, including the nuclear factor-κB, calcium, and Wingless (Wnt) pathways. One mechanism by which CO2 interacts with proteins to modulate cell signalling is through the reversible and nonenzymatic modification of α- N-terminal and lysine ε-amino groups to form the carbamate post-translational modification (PTM). Identifying carbamate PTMs is technically challenging because these modifications are readily reversible. However, emerging techniques have now made possible their identification and functional characterisation. Here, we review recent advances in experimental and computational methods to identify CO2-mediated PTMs.
nfc2fa81c3b99: Enzyme function is multidimensional, condition-dependent, and difficult to map at scale. Enzyme proximity sequencing (EP-Seq) is a deep mutational scanning method that combines a barcoded enzyme library, yeast surface display, fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), and high-throughput DNA sequencing to measure enzyme expression and catalytic activity.
n444578e6d824: By studying nearly half a million human genomes, this work shows that structural variants, large changes in DNA sequence greater than 50 base pairs, are an important and previously underrecognized source of human disease risk. The resulting resource reveals rare and regulatory structural variants linked to disease, providing insights into human biology and accelerating the development of medicines.
n3b869d82819c: Azo-morphine-3 (AM-3) is a photoswitchable ligand that toggles between low and high efficacy states to control mu-opioid receptor activity in vitro and in vivo both in the brain and periphery. AM-3 provides a powerful tool to probe the structural basis of opioid efficacy and enables spatiotemporally precise control of analgesia across pain models with reduced side effects compared with systemic drugs.
n85461ea325e3: Local cell-cell interactions give rise to emergent cellular patterns that encode ferroptosis-sensitive and -resistant fates and establish polarized lipid organization within cells. These coupled biochemical and biophysical properties enable self-organized cell populations to orient and confine otherwise isotropic, unbounded ferroptosis propagation, revealing a systems-level mechanism that regulates collective cell fate.
ncbd026f4cd08: Coleoid cephalopods edit their RNA at a level far beyond other animals, but the functional consequences to the proteome have been largely unknown. Proteomic detection of recoded sites reveals that single amino acid edits alter protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modification, and organelle function.
n775232b8c8e0: Pan et al. report tetraoxane-containing compounds WMK-1/2 as first-generation mitochondrial lipid peroxidation inducers that bypass GPX4- and retinol-mediated defenses to trigger a distinct “mito-ferroptosis” sub-pathway, demonstrating potent bioavailable tumor-suppressive activity across multiple in vivo models.
nd46b3bb0e829: A 22-tissue multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise is generated, detailing tissue-, sex-, and time-dependent molecular adaptations and cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling in skeletal muscle. The atlas reveals coordinated transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and metabolic remodeling across the body.
nd7cb15e418f6: Kong et al. present a comprehensive resource for benchmarking somatic variant detection across variant classes and allele fractions. Using HapMap mixtures and pangenome graphs, they establish standardized benchmarking sets for evaluating sequencing technologies and variant-calling methods.
n99aa8f82a6de: Ha et al. benchmark detection strategies for mosaic mutations with low variant allele fractions (VAFs) using short- and long-read whole-genome sequencing. By cross-validating Illumina-based calls against PacBio HiFi data using cell-line mixtures generated across five institutions, they construct stratified reference sets, define realistic detection limits, and establish best practices for genome-wide analysis of low-VAF (<2%) variants in non-cancer tissues.
nb3f3b8a0e865: Lana Mediavilla et al. present NeoBridge, a biophysics-informed machine learning ensemble that prioritizes immunogenic neoantigens. In pancreatic cancer, subclonal neoantigen load, not clonal load, associates with worse survival, suggesting that clonal architecture should inform vaccine target selection
n2363795e9ce4: Qu et al. show that the Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) protects against endometritis by promoting production of the microbial metabolite tyrosol, which reaches the uterus and suppresses inflammation. These findings reveal a metabolite-mediated gut-uterus axis linking the intestinal microbiota to reproductive health.
na9d16e158b7b: Meyers, Medina Evora, Molina Tijeras, et al. show that the colorectal cancer-associated oral bacterium Gemella morbillorum (Gm) promotes tumor progression. Colonization of the colon by Gm increases intestinal permeability, enables epithelial cell invasion, reshapes host lipid metabolism, and triggers DNA damage, collectively accelerating disease progression.
n2c6683ad4213: Predicting which patients will benefit from cancer immunotherapy remains challenging. Braun et al. use live tumor tissue from routine needle and forceps biopsies to measure ex vivo immunotherapy response. Results are consistent with clinical outcomes in a small patient cohort, including patients misclassified by current biomarker tests.
na92fadf8eee5: Wang et al. demonstrate that high-current transcranial temporal interference stimulation targeting sgACC alleviates depression safely and delivers stronger short-term therapeutic effects than low-current or sham stimulation.
nd6bebe49f738: Akay et al. use a genome-wide CRISPR screen to identify Wnt signaling as a regulator of lipid accumulation in APOE4 oligodendrocytes. Stimulating Wnt signaling by inhibiting GSK3B reduced lipid droplets and improved myelination in iPSC-derived brain organoids and APOE4;PS19 mice.
nee552d79d25c: Guo et al. develop a multiplex lineage-tracing platform to systematically profile fibroblasts across all five anatomical layers of the skin. They uncover a highly coordinated, multi-stage sequence of fibroblast mobilization and architectural reorganization during wound healing, demonstrating that cell-intrinsic programs predominate over local microenvironments to govern layer-specific contributions.
n302cf0a48a7a: Daniel L. Kastner, physician-scientist, geneticist, mentor, and scientific leader, transformed our understanding of human inflammatory disease. His death is a profound loss not only to the immunology community but also to the numerous patients and families whose illnesses he elucidated—and for whom, in many cases, he developed effective treatments. Called the “father of autoinflammatory diseases,” Dan did more than discover individual disorders: he defined an entirely new category of human disease.
n028466f3b40e: Metabolic reprogramming regulates immune cell function; however, how metabolic signals instruct early monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Yang et al. show that LDHA-dependent cytosolic NAD+ regeneration promotes selective HIF1α translation, supporting commitment to a protective NOS2+ macrophage fate and revealing a broader link between redox metabolism and cell fate decisions.
n856af4ff701e: Qin et al. demonstrate that extrachromosomal DNA hubs function as inherent electrochemical reactors. By non-enzymatically generating a localized antioxidant shield, these hubs protect themselves from oxidative damage. Disrupting this spatial redox balance triggers ecDNA degradation, exposing a distinct vulnerability in ecDNA-positive cancers.
nc1cdbc532110: Müller, Kolesnikova, Doudin, et al. reveal a structural mechanism for residue-specific nucleosome acetylation by capturing the MSL histone acetyltransferase during catalysis. Their findings provide a foundation for understanding how H4K16 acetylation links transcription to changes in chromatin structure, a mechanism essential for Drosophila dosage compensation and implicated in human disease.
ndda0bb09677c: Lyu et al. show that the interaction between the deubiquitinase OTULIN and the ubiquitin ligase LUBAC restrains LUBAC autoubiquitination and activity. Disrupting this interaction enhances Met1-linked ubiquitination at the TNF receptor complex, which increases NF-κB signaling and sensitizes mice to TNF-dependent toxicity. Thus, the OTULIN-LUBAC interaction restricts Met1-linked ubiquitin signaling.
nc4620e7122b1: A weakness in glycobiology research is the insufficient integration of approaches used to connect glycan structure to function. From glycogene knockouts to understanding glycan structures, dynamics, and interactions, to determining whether a single glycan structure underlies a specific cellular function, no single approach provides sufficient information to establish these relationships. We argue that resolving glycan structure–function relationships requires the integration of complementary approaches spanning genetics, analytical glycomics, glycoengineering, structural biology, and computational modelling. The field stands at a transition point: from cataloguing glycan structures to understanding their diverse roles in regulating the biology of health and disease. Such an integrated approach will be critical for translating structural glycan information into mechanistic insights and, ultimately, informed glycoengineering and therapeutic design.
n249258f20d07: In Arabidopsis, pseudoenzyme class II T6P synthase functions as a T6P sensor that directly represses the master metabolic regulator SnRK1, highlighting a conserved switch that couples carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis in plants.
n28047ded39fc: Phenotype measurement scale has long been known to impact genetic inference, yet it is often ignored in modern studies. Costantino et al. characterize how the choice of phenotype scale affects the results of common analyses. They find that it can change GWAS hits and PGS × E interactions and influence PGS performance in specific subgroups.
n4b53e510b405: Gao et al. identify protein kinase (PKR) as a non-canonical stimulator of interferon genes (STING) effector in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury. STING oligomerization at the endoplasmic reticulum drives PKR-S33 autophosphorylation and TBK1-independent IKK-NF-κB activation. This pathway induces LAMP3-dependent lysosomal cell death, and its inhibition attenuates epithelial injury.
nd7eab5a7939f: Why does performance pressure sometimes cause choking but sometimes elicit exceptional performance? We propose that pressure shifts the complexity of information-processing rules that guide action. Performance improves when shifts move processing toward task-matched complexity and deteriorates when they promote maladaptive simplification, overcomplexification, or the use of rules that exceed available processing resources.
nd3b305961c8f: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.
n2a01732cc6c8: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.
nf0f8318ec4c4: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.
n352689535a20: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.
nd9d7d6cec6b0: Oladeji et al. determined the cryo-EM structure of the TccCas13a ternary complex and leveraged structural insights to engineer a thermophilic Cas13a variant with 100-fold enhanced sensitivity. The engineered nuclease retains programmability and thermostability, enabling highly sensitive RNA detection in different biological matrices.
n577324ec4e19: Yang and colleagues show that low-intensity priming during rapid chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T manufacturing preserves T cell fitness while restraining inflammatory programming. PrimeCAR cells maintain stemness-associated and proliferative responses with reduced myeloid-activating inflammation, and early-phase studies in B cell malignancies demonstrate encouraging clinical activity with few severe cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) events.
n232536a222ef: Yuan et al. establish a scalable single-cell CRISPR platform in primary human HSPCs, linking 322 regulator perturbations to cell states and gene programs. The atlas identifies regulators associated with long-term repopulation and lineage-biased outputs and nominates PRDM10 as a candidate AML dependency.
n89e6ec2dfce9: Bai et al. reveal a PARP1-mediated m6A feedback mechanism involving IGF2BPs and the METTL3/METTL14 writer complex. They further show that combined targeting of ADP ribosylation and m6A leads to synergistic anti-tumor effects, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment.
n3cd9da96f6d5: Retrons help bacteria defend against phage by initiating a toxic response to restrict viral propagation. Here, Zhang et al. describe the non-canonical mechanism of Retron-Vpa2, which accumulates msDNA in response to phage triggers and regulates its toxic response on a translational level through a highly structured hybrid RNA.
n038f844d330f: Shin et al. present cryo-EM structures of the SPβ integrase along the integration and excision pathways that provide mechanistic insights addressing the long-standing questions of how large serine integrases enforce highly directional DNA recombination and how the cognate recombination directionality factor leads to a complete reversal of directionality.
n20f04c827951: Li et al. systematically map splicing within and between transposable elements (TEs) across cancers and define TEtrans, a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts. TEtrans display distinct regulatory programs and can function as oncogenic RNAs or encode immunogenic tumor antigens, expanding the functional landscape of TE reactivation in cancer.
n5d58caad6e4e: Lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease, and while targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved patient outcomes, 5-year overall survival remains poor at approximately 20%. Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) target tumors using a targeted antibody that delivers a cytotoxic payload with clinically proven antitumor activity, and over a dozen ADCs are under consideration for solid tumors. Recent clinical trial data in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer have led to FDA approval of three ADCs: trastuzumab deruxtecan for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-mutated disease, telisotuzumab vedotin for MET-overexpressing tumors, and datopotamab deruxtecan for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated disease. In this article, we review the trajectory of individual ADC targets in lung cancer, describe the latest clinical trial results, and discuss future innovations in ADC therapies and potential mechanisms of resistance.
nbd63ddd156f9: Höppner et al. show that disease-associated substitutions in PTH1R helix-8 selectively rewire receptor coupling to G proteins and βarrestin. Distinct mutations bias PTH1R engagement toward either Gαq or βarrestin pathways and impair Gαs activation. These findings reveal mutation-driven shifts in effector selectivity as a previously unrecognized mechanism in PTH1R-associated disease.
n718909ec8591: Wang et al. develop an oral metabolically engineered bacterial platform (EcN-HlpA-CGL [EHC]) for colorectal cancer immunotherapy, which triggers ferroptosis in colorectal cancer cells to boost immunogenicity, while the bacterial adjuvanticity reshapes the immunosuppressive microenvironment. This approach activates both systemic and gut mucosal immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic tumor growth and metastasis.
nf3a2a5dfdcc8: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells are heterogeneous, but how pathogenic subsets drive relapse in allergic dermatitis remains unclear. Asahina et al. identify a pathogenic CXCR6+ CD4+ TRM subset sustained through CXCL16-dependent clustering with CD301b+ cDC2s, revealing the TRM-DC niche as a potential therapeutic target for allergic dermatitis.
n6bc218949b2c: How metabolic enzyme levels are regulated is poorly understood. Studying the tryptophan (Trp)-metabolizing enzyme TDO2, Thielen et al. discover a CK2 kinase-β-TrCP E3 ligase pathway that regulates stability in response to substrate availability. Trp occupation of an exosite restricts degron accessibility, whereas low Trp releases the degron for phosphorylation-ubiquitylation-mediated degradation.
n695f93081a8a: Liang et al. identify phytanoyl-CoA dioxygenase domain containing 1 (PHYHD1) as a tumor suppressor that regulates protein production in kidney cancer. Loss of PHYHD1 promotes disease progression by increasing ceramide transporter 1 (CERT1) production, uncovering a regulatory pathway that may help predict patient outcomes and provide a therapeutic opportunity for PHYHD1-deficient tumors.
nf720614dfc33: Bonsor et al. determined the crystal structure of the KRAS-BRAF(RBD-CRD) complex, revealing reduced KRAS engagement by BRAF(CRD) compared with CRAF(CRD). They further show that the BRAF-specific region (BSR) attenuates RBD binding to KRAS, while inclusion of the CRD partially relieves this inhibition.
nf50730d9c221: Predictions of cysteine reactivity rely heavily on acidity (pKa) data from dilute solutions. However, the intracellular milieu is crowded and dynamic, with substrates, cofactors, and metabolites that modulate reactivity, thereby affecting cell signaling and metabolic adaptation. This forum argues that Cys pKa values are necessary but insufficient, proposing an integrated, microenvironment-dependent framework.
nc7255fb8e658: RNA fingerprinting is a statistical framework that infers causal regulators from single-cell experiments by mapping their transcriptional responses onto reference perturbation dictionaries.
n339bcbe92910: Chromatin reader inhibitors require robust cellular assays for target-engagement profiling. Recchia et al. develop modular Acyl-eCR reporters that enable scalable live-cell measurement of bromodomain inhibitor specificity and PROTAC activity, providing a versatile platform for chromatin-targeted drug discovery.
n3623de86684d: Symmans et al. review how artificial intelligence supports RNA therapeutic development in precision oncology, spanning multi-omics target prioritization and RNA design to delivery, patient stratification, manufacturing, and clinical translation. They distinguish clinically supported applications from preclinical and speculative approaches, outlining validation, governance, and regulatory requirements.
n93ed1f40f36f: Citrano, Maheswari Jawahar et al. develop sensitive immunoassays using second-generation polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies against HDGFL2-CE proteins and show that their levels in brain tissue associate with pTDP-43 pathology, earlier symptom onset, and shorter survival in patients with FTLD-TDP and FTLD-TDP/MND.
n1236e016d64e: Cabello-Yeves et al. use longitudinal metagenomic analysis of mother-infant dyads to show that infant gut phageomes diversify during the first year of life and are associated with feeding-related variables and maternal microbial reservoirs. Persistent bifidophages dominate early communities, highlighting the potential relevance of phages in microbiome-targeted early-life interventions.
n2459946c13b1: Zhao et al. show that circulating TCDCA associates with Parkinson’s disease severity and that TCDCA administration worsens neurovascular and motor outcomes in mice. VSMC TGR5 deletion and BSH-active L. reuteri interventions implicate a microbiota-regulated TCDCA-BBB pathway while defining its translational limitations.
nb2dff07df845: Klich et al. use a hydrogel to deliver immunotherapy combinations intratumorally and peritumorally. Rational selection of the site of administration drives tumor clearance and long-term survivors.
ncfb38586f394: Lymphatic vessel networks remodel during infection to regulate antigen and immune cell dynamics, yet whether these changes impact humoral immunity remains unknown. Mudianto et al. demonstrate that lymph node lymphangiogenesis encapsulates activating germinal centers to constrain their size, which enhances clonal selection and protective antibody responses, establishing lymphatic vessels as structural determinants of germinal center fitness.
nbb50e569c598: Terekhova et al. assemble a single-cell PBMC atlas of 8 datasets, 2,609 individuals, and over 12 million cells to dissect variable and conserved features of human immune aging. CD8+ Tem GZMK+ to GZMB+ ratio distinguishes healthy from disease-associated trajectories and predicts mortality risk. This work provides a clinically relevant marker for monitoring human aging.
n6591ddf170c1: Translational perturbations trigger ubiquitination and turnover of 40S ribosomes, yet how these events are coupled remains unclear. Shah et al. reveal that RIOK3 remodels ubiquitinated 40S subunits, exposing the 3′ end of 18S rRNA for uridylation and subsequent DIS3L2-mediated degradation. These findings link ribosomal protein ubiquitination to selective rRNA turnover.
nb1e417dab41f: 40S ribosomes are degraded in diverse stress conditions. Diehl et al. find that in response to stress, TUT7 is recruited to ubiquitylated 40S ribosomes and adds 3′ oligo(U) tails to the 18S rRNA. Iterative uridylation and 3′-5′ decay by the exonuclease DIS3L2 drive 18S rRNA and ultimately 40S ribosome degradation.
n6ba87c7edd62: Protein phosphorylation is a central and reversible mechanism regulating virtually all cellular processes and is classically mediated by the canonical protein kinome and phosphatome. However, beyond their traditional roles as metabolic catalysts, a subset of metabolic enzymes also exhibits noncanonical ‘moonlighting’ activities as protein kinases or phosphatases, directly linking metabolic states to phosphorylation-dependent signaling. These unexpected functions of enzymes involved in glucose, fructose, lipid, nucleotide, and creatine metabolism influence a broad spectrum of cellular processes, including chromatin remodeling, transcription, cell cycle progression, metabolism, autophagy, cell survival and death, and immune responses. As a result, metabolic enzymes are increasingly recognized as key regulators that bridge cellular metabolism and signaling networks, with important implications for both normal physiology and disease.
